title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners
authors: A. Radford, J. Wu, R. Child, D. Luan, D. Amodei, I. Sutskever
before: Pretrained models needed a fine-tuning stage and labelled data for each task.
problem: Could scale alone make a language model do tasks it was never trained on?
breakthrough: 1.5B parameters trained on WebText, performing translation, summarisation and QA zero-shot from prompts alone.
why: The first real evidence for the scaling hypothesis, and the origin of the staged-release norm for risky models.
next: Scaling laws formalised the trend; GPT-3 took it two orders of magnitude further.
inherits: Prompting as the interface, and byte-level BPE tokenization.
